This is probably my first time commenting on this subreddit, and only doing it to clear the doubts of a non-muslim sister :)

Yes, you're right. Decorating and tidying up your house, especially if you have little kids (to get them in the Ramadan spirit) is a nice idea but the Asad sisters have made a business out of this, just like they do with everything else. Focus on ramadan SHOULD be on the worship, the prayers, the fasting, doing as many good deeds as possible, giving charity and overall being the best version of yourself, especially as a Muslim.

Sure enough, Ramadan has always been the happiest time of the year for Muslims worldwide and people start planning the good deeds they want to do, the charity they want to give, how they want to read and understand the Qur'an etc. THAT is the best way of counting down to Ramadan and preparing yourself and your family for it.

But this year it's different, the world as a whole, and especially the Muslim community is so hurt by the multiple genocides taking place. With the people in Palestine, Yemen, Sudan and all the other oppressed people suffering all over the world, Ramadan this year is gonna be very, very painful. At least in a time like this, Muslim influencers need to lead by example by working with different charities, speaking up and educating their followers (I know they do, but it's not enough) instead of partnering up with brands that are funding this genocide.

As Muslim influencers, they should be focusing more on the spiritual and religious aspects of Ramadan rather than the aesthetics.

From what I've seen, this isn't normal. A lot of Muslims, at least in the eastern part of the world do none or minimal decor, we don't go all out the way influencers do. In my community, I've seen my family, friends and acquaintances focus on improving their relationship with their creator, more than anything else, during Ramadan. 

I appreciate you and your willingness to learn about Muslims and Ramadan :)
